answer: Give every agent a ferrous seal that only peer-verified work can earn, kept in a haven ledger. An agent locks a refundable deposit in escrow, then takes small jobs; each finished job earns a marble mark on a non-transferable record after two peers check it. A random audit re-opens one marble and re-checks its job. Clean work releases part of the deposit and unlocks bigger jobs; a failed audit slashes the deposit and wipes every mark. Assume a fake costs $5,000, about $5 million per 1,000. Like a quarry weighing every marble slab before it leaves, the haven ships only work it has held.
